segments: The 26th [chapter], the 18th dynasty.
Arab kings.
And he had an inflammation in his bowels,
and he also had epilepsy,
which follows the colic pain.
And he ordered that mithridate be compounded for him,
and one of his servants put into it an excess amount of opium.
And when he took from it several times,
his natural warmth was extinguished.
And from then on he neglected to treat himself, and he used to say:
"The governor who used to govern my body has failed and grown weak,
and it is no longer able to govern."
And he remained thus for a few days,
and he died and was buried in the city of Hamadan at the age of fifty-eight years.
And in the year one thousand three hundred and forty-nine [of the Greeks, 1038 AD],
429 of the Arabs [AH]:
The Ghuzz came again to Armenia,
and they wrought a great slaughter among the Kurds and the Arabs there,
and took much plunder.
And from there they came to the city of Urmia in Azerbaijan,
and they plundered the region,
and killed many of the Kurds of that mountain,
who had come down and engaged them.
And when the Emir Ibn Waththab,
who ruled over Syria and Armenia, saw
that he was unable to meet two enemies, the Romans and the Turks,
he made peace with the Romans.
And Edessa remained to the Romans,
and they took full possession of it and established priests in it.
And in that year the Ghuzz captured the city of Maragha,
and burned the great mosque in it,
and they killed and captured many of its inhabitants.
Then the bands of mountain Kurds gathered together,
and prevailed against the Ghuzz,
and drove them out of Azerbaijan.
And they returned again to Khorasan,
and captured the city of Tus,
and killed in it about one hundred thousand souls,
and outside, on the roads and in the villages, about twenty thousand,
and they took about one hundred and fifty thousand captives.
And Subashi, the ruler of Khorasan, came against them with thirty thousand horsemen,
and they broke him and put him to flight.
And they came to the city of Nishapur,
and when they were intending to pillage it,
Tughril Beg restrained them,
because the fast of the Arabs was approaching.
And al-Qaim the Caliph also sent an envoy to them and censured them,
saying: How is it
that, being Arabs [i.e., Muslims {OCR? - or Tayyaye}],
they do such things to the people of their own faith? And because after the fast they were going to destroy Nishapur,
